--- a/minbpe/_heap.py
+++ b/minbpe/_heap.py
@@ -0,0 +1,72 @@
+"""
+Long-sequence merge application, loaded on first use (most callers never
+need it, so it stays off the package import path).
+"""
+from heapq import heapify, heappop, heappush
+
+
+def _apply_merges_heap(ids, merges):
+    """
+    Same result as base.apply_merges, for long sequences: a doubly linked list
+    over the original positions plus a heap of (rank, position) entries for
+    every mergeable adjacent pair. Entries are validated lazily when popped (a
+    pair whose tokens changed is recomputed), and each round pops all entries
+    of the minimal rank in position order, i.e. sequence order. The first
+    valid one picks the pair (same as the first-seen minimal pair); its
+    occurrences are merged left to right, skipping overlaps, exactly like merge().
+    """
+    merges_get = merges.get
+    n = len(ids)
+    val = list(ids)
+    nxt = list(range(1, n + 1)) # n means "no next"
+    prv = list(range(-1, n - 1)) # -1 means "no previous"
+    heap = [(r, i) for i, r in enumerate(map(merges_get, zip(val, val[1:])))
+            if r is not None]
+    heapify(heap)
+    while heap:
+        r = heap[0][0]
+        pair = None
+        last = -1
+        merged = []
+        rest = []
+        while heap and heap[0][0] == r:
+            p = heappop(heap)[1]
+            if p == last:
+                continue # duplicate entry (pops come out in position order)
+            last = p
+            v = val[p]
+            if v is None:
+                continue # position was merged away
+            q = nxt[p]
+            if q == n:
+                continue
+            pr = (v, val[q])
+            if merges_get(pr) != r:
+                continue # stale entry
+            if pair is None:
+                pair = pr
+            elif pr != pair:
+                rest.append(p) # another pair with the same rank: later round
+                continue
+            val[p] = r
+            val[q] = None
+            q2 = nxt[q]
+            nxt[p] = q2
+            if q2 < n:
+                prv[q2] = p
+            merged.append(p)
+        for p in rest:
+            heappush(heap, (r, p))
+        for p in merged:
+            a = prv[p]
+            if a >= 0:
+                rk = merges_get((val[a], r))
+                if rk is not None:
+                    heappush(heap, (rk, a))
+            b = nxt[p]
+            if b < n:
+                rk = merges_get((r, val[b]))
+                if rk is not None:
+                    heappush(heap, (rk, p))
+    return [v for v in val if v is not None]
+

+"""Encoding-only helpers, loaded on first use (off the package import path)."""
+from heapq import heapify, heappop, heappush
+from .basic import _replace_table
+
+
+def _chunk_table(merges):
+    # basic._replace_table, or None if the 0xff chunk separator could clash
+    # with a merge (as a pair token or as a minted token)
+    if not merges:
+        return None
+    table = _replace_table(merges)
+    if table is None:
+        return None
+    for ps, c in table:
+        if "\xff" in ps or c == "\xff":
+            return None
+    return table
+
+
+def _split_specials(text, special):
+    # re.split of the escaped tokens alternation (non-empty tokens), no regex
+    parts = []
+    pos = 0
+    while True:
+        best = -1
+        for k in special:
+            i = text.find(k, pos)
+            if i != -1 and (best == -1 or i < best):
+                best, tok = i, k
+        if best == -1:
+            parts.append(text[pos:])
+            return parts
+        parts += text[pos:best], tok
+        pos = best + len(tok)
+
+
+def _apply_merges_heap(ids, merges):
+    """
+    Same result as base.apply_merges, for long sequences: a doubly linked list
+    over the positions plus a lazily validated heap of (rank, position); each
+    round merges the minimal rank's first pair left to right, like merge().
+    """
+    merges_get = merges.get
+    n = len(ids)
+    val = list(ids)
+    nxt = list(range(1, n + 1)) # n means "no next"
+    prv = list(range(-1, n - 1)) # -1 means "no previous"
+    heap = [(r, i) for i, r in enumerate(map(merges_get, zip(val, val[1:])))
+            if r is not None]
+    heapify(heap)
+    while heap:
+        r = heap[0][0]
+        pair = None
+        last = -1
+        merged = []
+        rest = []
+        while heap and heap[0][0] == r:
+            p = heappop(heap)[1]
+            if p == last:
+                continue # duplicate entry (pops come out in position order)
+            last = p
+            v = val[p]
+            if v is None:
+                continue # position was merged away
+            q = nxt[p]
+            if q == n:
+                continue
+            pr = (v, val[q])
+            if merges_get(pr) != r:
+                continue # stale entry
+            if pair is None:
+                pair = pr
+            elif pr != pair:
+                rest.append(p) # another pair with the same rank: later round
+                continue
+            val[p] = r
+            val[q] = None
+            q2 = nxt[q]
+            nxt[p] = q2
+            if q2 < n:
+                prv[q2] = p
+            merged.append(p)
+        for p in rest:
+            heappush(heap, (r, p))
+        for p in merged:
+            a = prv[p]
+            if a >= 0:
+                rk = merges_get((val[a], r))
+                if rk is not None:
+                    heappush(heap, (rk, a))
+            b = nxt[p]
+            if b < n:
+                rk = merges_get((r, val[b]))
+                if rk is not None:
+                    heappush(heap, (rk, p))
+    return [v for v in val if v is not None]

I moved the encode-only helpers out of the import path. _apply_merges_heap from base.py and _chunk_table and _split_specials from regex.py went into a new minbpe/_heap.py, imported lazily at their only call sites (apply_merges for long inputs, RegexTokenizer._encode_state, RegexTokenizer.encode). The code bodies are unchanged. Training never touches them, but they were compiled on every import.

My first try only moved the base.py helper. It was rejected with train_ir ratio 0.9908 against a required 0.9900. Outputs were identical. Moving the regex.py helpers too got accepted in my sandbox: train_ir went from 362386785 to 357872331, ratio 0.9875, and encode_ir stayed at 0.9998. It touched 3 files and 199 lines. I submitted it and it is queued for replay.

The train_ir benchmark seems to count import and compile cost, so dead weight at module load is a real target. The margin is thin, though.

Next I would look for other module-level work that training never needs, and I would profile the training loop itself for a larger win.
